Welcome to Google Antigravity

Welcome to
Google Antigravity!

Google Antigravity is the platform built for the era of agentic development. Co-optimized with Gemini, Antigravity brings the frontier of model intelligence directly into your workflows.

No matter which surface you start with, you get the same agentic experience, complete with multi-agent orchestration, interactive artifacts, and ecosystem integration.

Explore the Antigravity Ecosystem

Antigravity 2.0

Agent-first mission control

Antigravity 2.0 is an agent-first, standalone desktop application made for developer workflows, where you experience the frontier of Gemini's model intelligence. Built to scale as models evolve, it serves as your central command center to orchestrate parallel subagents across multiple projects, automate routine tasks with Scheduled Tasks, and manage your entire software development workflow.

Learn more →

Antigravity CLI

Antigravity agent in your terminal

Designed for developers who live in the command line. Work directly with autonomous agents from your terminal to execute background tasks, manage workspace context, and run specialized slash commands.

Learn more →

Antigravity IDE

Fully-featured agentic IDE

Combines your traditional code editor experience with powerful agentic capabilities. Enjoy context-aware Agents and rich visual artifact review right inside your workspace.

Learn more →

Antigravity SDK

Build, customize, and deploy antigravity agents

Build custom AI agents that autonomously read files, run commands, edit code, and ingest multimodal assets. The Agent SDK abstracts away the complex machinery of running an AI agent, including state management, tool execution, and backend communication. It gives you the exact same tools, agent loop, and context management that power the Google Antigravity products, programmable directly in Python.

Learn more →

Shared agentic capabilities

Parallel Teams of Agents

Delegate subtasks to subagents, running background research, code edits, and browser tests in parallel without collision.

Interactive Artifacts

Artifacts give you visibility into what the agent is doing and what it has built. Leave feedback directly on any artifact to guide the agent and steer your project in real time.

Slash Commands

Access a rich library of shortcuts to quickly trigger tools like aligning on requirements (via /grill-me) and spawning asynchronous side tasks (via /btw). Custom skills defined in your workspace automatically register as native slash commands across surfaces.

Start Building with Google Antigravity

Need help getting started or want to see what’s new?

Explore the Documentation → | Release Notes →

As a reminder, don’t submit sensitive or personal information to Google Antigravity.

To help with quality, safety, and to improve our products, human reviewers may read, annotate, and process that data. Learn more about data use.

We noticed a few 429 Too Many Requests errors when sending batch webhook payloads yesterday evening around 8:00 PM UTC.

Could you clarify whether the current rate limit is 100 req/sec per workspace or if there is an hourly burst allowance? We want to tune our retry queues accordingly.

Staff Infrastructure Engineer

analysis.suggested_action: Acknowledge inquiry and provide rate limit specifications with documentation link.

suggestedReply.content:

For high-volume batch payloads, we recommend enabling exponential backoff with jitter on your retry queues. I would be happy to share our webhook best practices guide if helpful.

Best regards,
Alex Vance
Head of Operations, MailPilot
